findings.description: The program-code check relies on a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. The set does not establish which changes to the application image must be detected.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-004 as blocking and obtain the integrity-check acceptance criteria needed to verify the requirement.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires milliseconds since start, but OP-SYS-006 leaves the timestamp origin and wrap behavior undefined. Expected report values across resets and counter wrap cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-006 as blocking and obtain the timestamp origin and wrap behavior.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but CON-SUP-112 does not define the entity for the code 8 watchdog-reset report.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the entity value for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined, so the expected GET STATUS response cannot be determined for a given operating and reset history.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-005 as blocking and obtain the state values and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The requirement demands detection at expiry while accepting completion at that instant. OP-SYS-009 leaves treatment of a completion in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry unspecified, preventing a boundary verdict.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and resolve the expiry boundary and measurement treatment.

findings.description: The requirement accepts a start at the limit and detects a start later than the limit, but OP-SYS-009 leaves unresolved how starts in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry are distinguished.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and define the measurable late-start boundary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the classified reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-031 sends it in a start-up message, while SYS-SUP-033 through SYS-SUP-035 provide no request that returns it.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-002 and specify how the service tool reads the classified reset cause.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the fault report to be transmitted after safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-023 specifies a 10 ms deadline from detection, and SYS-SUP-027 requires the report before reset; neither requires transmission after entry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-008 and specify the required ordering and compatible timing of safe-state entry and report transmission.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but SYS-SUP-026 defines entities only for codes 1 through 7. CON-SUP-112 also defines codes 8 and 9.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-003 and specify the report entity for codes 8 and 9.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 detects a late-start fault only when the task starts, while CON-SUP-105 measures the reaction from expiry of a timing limit. OP-SYS-010 defers the detection instant for a task that never starts, leaving its timely response unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-010 as blocking and resolve detection and reaction timing when a task has not started by its limit.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the outputs and status signal to be driven low within 50 ms, but does not require them to remain low until reset for an unlatched fault. SYS-SUP-046 provides that hold only while the safe state is latched, leaving the recovery sequence in STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the safe-state outputs and status are maintained from entry until the recovery reset for an unlatched fault.
